title: Territory selector and fallback resolution refactor
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Background: The current routing policy engine mixes region/tier selection, model-variant fallbacks, and legacy match rules in a set of ad-hoc validators and runtime checks. This has resulted in surprising behavior during failover, brittle rollouts across Dedicated/Private deployments, and a proliferation of per-customer workarounds.

Objective: Refactor the policy intake and validation pipeline into a compact, testable composer that separates three concerns: (1) territory selection (region/zone affinity and legal boundaries), (2) tier steering (capacity/cost-driven route weighting, SLAs), and (3) fallback lattice (ordered model-variant fallbacks with compatibility constraints). Deliver a schema-first validator and a staged migration plan that preserves existing semantics while enabling future expressive policies.

Success criteria:
- A canonical JSON/YAML schema expressing selectors, tier policies, and fallback chains with clear invariants.
- New validator rejects ambiguous or underspecified rules (e.g., conflicting region include/exclude).
- Compatibility shim accepts existing policy DSLs and emits warnings for non-idiomatic constructs rather than hard failures.
- End-to-end tests covering canary rollouts, cross-region failover, and tier preemption.
- No customer-facing regressions for high-traffic customers during staged rollouts (validation gated behind feature flag and rollout windows).

Non-goals: full DSL rewrite or runtime routing execution overhaul. This ticket focuses on intake, static validation, and migration tooling; runtime router optimization comes in a follow-up.

Design approach:
- Introduce a Policy Composer that normalizes incoming configs into a canonical IR. The IR will encode: region sets (with explicit precedence), tier predicates (capacity, cost tiers, SLA tags), and fallback graphs (acyclic, version-compatibility annotated).
- Implement a schema using JSON Schema + custom semantic validators for constraints that cannot be expressed declaratively (e.g., transitive compatibility in fallback graphs).
- Build an adapter that translates the legacy DSL into the new IR. The adapter will surface a graded diagnostics stream (ok/warn/error) to help customers migrate.
- Add a lightweight property-based fuzzer that generates malformed or edge-case routing specs to validate validator robustness.

Migration plan:
1) Add Composer behind a feature flag in intake service; new policies can opt-in.
2) Run adapter on existing stored policies to produce a migration report. Surface customers with warnings.
3) Offer a staged enforcement window: warn-only (2 weeks) -> soft-fail (canary) -> hard-fail (global).

Testing & observability:
- Unit tests for schema edge cases and adapter heuristics.
- Integration tests that simulate region outage and verify fallback selection correctness and SLA preservation.
- Telemetry: policy-validation metrics (pass/warn/fail rates), adapter-warning categories, and a sample of transformed IRs (redacted) for auditing.

Rollout & ops:
- Canary group: internal dev accounts + five low-traffic customers.
- Monitoring playbook: validation error spike alert, rollback on >2% of traffic impacted, manual review for flagged policies.

Risks:
- Overly strict validations could break existing customer policies. Mitigation: long warn window, robust adapter heuristics.
- Complex fallback graphs could be expensive to validate at intake. Mitigation: incremental validators and caching of validated IRs.

Alternatives considered:
- Big-bang runtime switch: rejected due to high blast radius.
- Keep validators but add more unit tests: insufficient for long-term expressivity and maintainability.

Artifacts & links: Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/def-policy-composer (design+examples); Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-composer/pull/72 (WIP); Internal test harness: gs://redwood-test-harness/smart-routing/fallback-sims/2026-02.

Next steps: finalize canonical schema and begin implementation of the adapter + semantic validator. Coordinate with Console team to expose validation warnings in the policy editor UX.

2026-03-02 - Diego Martinez: Implemented initial adapter proof-of-concept that translates legacy 'regional_affinity' blocks into 'territory' sets. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-composer/pull/72

2026-03-05 - Sofia Chen (reviewer): Review notes - require clearer diagnostics for 'mutually exclusive' region rules and add an invariant check for cycles in fallback graphs. Left inline comments on PR.
